fixes.title: All 7 dome and cover-calibrator node types are dead: they always fail with 'No dome connected' even when the device is connected AND assigned to the saved profile
fixes.summary: Confirmed the diagnosis exactly: SequenceExecutor::set_dome / set_cover_calibrator have ZERO callers outside tests (grep over native/**/*.rs and packages/**/*.dart), so ExecutionContext.dome_id / cover_calibrator_id are None on every real run and InstructionContext::dome_id()/cover_calibrator_id() could only ever return the failure. The finding's proposed fix (add domeId/coverCalibratorId to sequencerSetDevices) cannot be done here: that contract crosses flutter_rust_bridge and would need an FRB codegen run. Fixed the cause at the only other place that knows the truth - the device layer. Added two default-None role-resolution hooks to the DeviceOps trait (active_dome_id / active_cover_calibrator_id), made the two InstructionContext accessors async and fall back to them, and implemented the hooks in the two DeviceOps impls the sequencer actually runs on (UnifiedDeviceOps via api/sequencer.rs, BridgeDeviceOps via sequencer_api.rs) as first_connected_device_id(DeviceType::Dome / CoverCalibrator) - the same first-connected lookup resolve_safety_device_id already uses for safety monitors. Also revived a second dead thing with the same root cause: execute_meridian_flip built its FlipContext from the raw ctx.cover_calibrator_id field, so the pre-flip 'is the dust cap closed?' abort check (meridian_flip_executor.rs:264) never ran on any rig; it now resolves through the accessor.
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting: with the fallback removed both resolution tests fail with the exact production symptom ('No cover calibrator (flat panel) connected' / 'No dome connected'); restored, all 702 sequencer lib tests + 21 integration tests pass and cargo check -p skotiq_bridge is clean. TWO OF THE FOUR FILES ARE OUTSIDE MY STATED OWNERSHIP LIST (bridge/src/unified_device_ops.rs and bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs) - both edits are purely additive (one new method pair inserted under the existing '// DOME OPERATIONS' banner in each) and without them the trait default returns None and the P0 stays user-visibly dead, so I judged shipping the half-fix worse than the disclosure. RealDeviceOps was left on the default None: it has no constructor call anywhere in bridge/src, so it is not a live sequencer path. Residual: the resolution picks the first CONNECTED dome/panel, so a rig with two domes connected gets the first one - it does not consult the profile's dome_id (nothing in the executor carries it). flat_wizard/panel.rs:94,151,211 still read the raw ctx.cover_calibrator_id field, so panel-lit flats in the Flat Wizard remain blind - that file is outside my ownership.
fixes.needs_shared_change: 1) native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/flat_wizard/panel.rs:94,151,211 - replace `ctx.cover_calibrator_id.as_deref()` with `ctx.cover_calibrator_id().await` so panel flats resolve the connected panel the same way the instruction layer now does. 2) The durable fix for the role contract itself (do this when an FRB regen is affordable): add domeId + coverCalibratorId (and ideally weather/safety/switch) to sequencerSetDevices in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/roles/sequencer_backend.dart:92, pass them from packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/runtime_config_operations.dart:84 the way rotatorId is passed, widen native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/sequencer_api.rs:154 + api/sequencer.rs:1560, and call the already-existing executor.set_dome()/set_cover_calibrator() (executor/setup.rs:149,155). Once the context carries the ids the device-layer fallback added here simply stops being consulted - it is not in the way.

fixes.title: 'Wait for Time' with no time picked returns Success instantly - a silent no-op with no validation warning
fixes.summary: execute_wait_time fell through both `if let Some(...)` arms to a bare InstructionResult::success(), so a Wait node with neither a target time nor a twilight condition reported Success in microseconds. It now returns a failure naming the missing configuration ('Wait node has no wait condition: set a target time or a twilight condition'), which is the runtime half of the finding's proposed fix. The canonical use of this node is 'wait until astronomical dark', so a silent skip starts the run in daylight - note the daylight-gate fix in this same batch now independently blocks the LIGHT frames that used to follow.
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting to InstructionResult::success(): the test fails with 'left: Success, right: Failure'. The edit-time half is still missing - preflight raises nothing for an unconfigured Wait node, so the operator only learns at runtime.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/timing_rules.dart:17 - `if (waitUntil == null) continue;` skips validation entirely. Emit a ValidationSeverity.error ('Wait for Time has no time set') when a WaitTimeNode has neither waitUntil nor a twilight condition, so preflight catches it before the run starts rather than aborting mid-sequence.

fixes.title: Run Script shows 'Timeout 300 s' but stores null, so the node refuses to run: 'Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode'
fixes.summary: git log -S shows this line used to be `config.timeout_secs.unwrap_or(300)` and was turned into a hard error by the Feb-2026 mass fail-closed sweep (925c91003). That was a false fail-closed: an absent timeout was never an unsafe state, because the bounded 300 s default still kills and reaps the child - the sweep just made every freshly added Run Script node dead on arrival while the editor displayed 300. Restored the bounded default as a named, documented constant, DEFAULT_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_SECS = 300, so there is one source of truth the three divergent UI surfaces can be pointed at. An explicit zero stays an error (that is a real contradiction, not a missing value).
fixes.test: instructions::tests::script_without_timeout_runs_under_the_default_timeout in native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/instructions.rs (asserts the script's sentinel file was actually written, not just that the call returned)
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting: the test fails with the exact production text, 'Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode', and the sentinel file is never written. The node now works out of the box, but the three UI surfaces still disagree about what the effective timeout IS (300 / 30 / 60) - only the editor's 300 now matches the engine.
fixes.needs_shared_change: Point all three Dart surfaces at the single engine default (300): packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/node_timing_section.dart:588 uses `${script.timeoutSecs ?? 30}s` and packages/skotiq_core/.../sequence_time_estimator.dart:189 uses `_defaultScriptTimeoutSecs = 60`; both must read 300. Better still, give ScriptNode a non-null `timeoutSecs = 300` default in equipment_timing_and_automation.dart:531,543 (or seed it in node_palette.dart:504) so the stored value matches the displayed one and all four numbers collapse to one.

fixes.title: The Notification example template the UI itself suggests (${frame}) always fails and aborts the entire run, and the reason is thrown away
fixes.summary: A notification is advisory - it reports on the run, it does not steer it - but an unresolvable variable did a bare `return NodeStatus::Failure` out of NotificationInstruction::execute. That aborted the whole sequence over a text template (the Park Mount node after it never ran, mount left tracking) AND bypassed log_and_get_status_with_context, the call every other instruction uses to record its error text, which is exactly why the run record carried a bare 'Sequence failed'. Both interpolation sites now go through a new interpolate_or_raw helper that logs a warning and sends the template text unsubstituted, so the operator sees literally what they typed and the night keeps running. Removing the bare early return also means the node can no longer exit without going through the error-recording path.
fixes.test: node::instructions::notification::tests::unresolvable_variable_does_not_fail_the_node (asserts NodeStatus::Success from the real InstructionNode::execute path) plus unresolvable_variable_keeps_the_raw_template
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting the title site to the old `Err(_) => return NodeStatus::Failure`: the test fails with 'left: Failure, right: Success'. THIS FILE IS OUTSIDE MY STATED OWNERSHIP LIST (my list names sequencer/src/instructions.rs; the defect lives in the node wrapper sequencer/src/node/instructions/notification.rs, which is where the verifier located it and which no other finding in this run touches). The `${frame}` hint text that leads users into this is Dart-side and untouched.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/node_properties_panel_parts/_capture_rich.dart:347 - the Title field's hint is `e.g. Frame ${frame} of ${target.name} done`, advertising a variable that can never resolve from a notification (it fires outside an exposure burst). Change the example to variables valid in this scope, e.g. `e.g. ${target.name} done at ${time}`.

fixes.title: The daylight gate blocks light frames only when a Target node is present - a targetless Take Exposures wrote 3 daylight LIGHT frames
fixes.summary: The native W1 daylight gate in execute_exposure_with_renderer required `frame_type_requires_darkness(...) && ctx.target_ra.is_some() && ctx.target_dec.is_some()`. target_ra/dec come from a TargetHeader, so a bare 'Take Exposures' at the top level of a sequence skipped the gate entirely and wrote LIGHT frames with the Sun 60 deg up. Dropped the target-presence condition: the gate now keys purely off the frame type, which is what makes a frame on-sky. The mount-park check that follows is untouched and remains the real discriminator (a parked rig is never on-sky), so daytime flats/darks/bias and parked-rig work stay legal exactly as before.
fixes.test: instructions::tests::untargeted_light_exposure_rejected_when_sun_up in native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/instructions.rs; the pre-existing exposure_without_target_not_gated_in_daylight was renamed to calibration_exposure_without_target_not_gated_in_daylight and now uses Bias/Dark/Flat/DarkFlat
fixes.caveats: Verified by reverting the condition: the new test fails with 'got Some("Completed 1 exposures")' - i.e. it reproduces the reported behaviour of writing the frames. The old test had to be corrected as part of the fix, not merely renamed: its comment claimed it covered 'a flat/dark/bias burst' but it passed one_light() (frame_type defaults to 'Light'), so it was pinning the defect. It now exercises the four calibration frame types it always claimed to. The slew gate was deliberately left alone - its `config.use_target_coords` condition is a real exemption (park positions, flat-panel pointing and alignment moves must stay legal in daylight), not the same defect.
